language.title: Metadata language
language.description: Languages of the metadata of the data source. Select from the EU Publications Office language authority vocabulary.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name given to the dataset in a generic term. The name should be a meaningful, unique and unambiguous label.

description.title: Description
description.description: Information about the dataset as a free-text description. It is used only for a brief overview.
description.default: My Data Source contains mobility data about mobility things.

publisher_name.title: Publisher name
publisher_name.description: An entity (company and person) that publishes the dataset. This entity is responsible for the provisioning of a dataset. The entity also concludes a contract, if applicable.

mobility_theme_category.title: Mobility theme category
mobility_theme_category.description: Mobility-related theme categories (i.e., a specific subject, category, or type) of the delivered content. A dataset may be associated with multiple themes. A theme is important for data seekers who are interested in a particular type of data content. The theme is described via the mobilitydcatap:mobility-theme vocabulary in two hierarchy levels: this is the 1st level describing the classification of the data content on an aggregated level.

mobility_theme_subcategory.title: Mobility theme subcategory
mobility_theme_subcategory.description: Mobility-related theme sub-categories (i.e., a specific subject, category, or type) of the delivered content. The theme is described via the mobilitydcatap:mobility-theme vocabulary in two hierarchy levels: this is the 2nd level, an optional field detailing the category previously entered via one or several sub-categories.

accrual_periodicity.title: Accrual periodicity
accrual_periodicity.description: How often the delivered content is updated. This information tells a data consumer how often it is updated on the data platform, so the data consumer might align the frequency of data retrieval accordingly. For dynamic data feeds, the frequency should correspond to the technical upload / data push frequency. For static datasets, it should correspond to the expected change frequency. Select from the EU Publications Office frequency authority vocabulary.

spatial_coverage.description: A geographic region that is covered by the delivered content. It can be represented via a geocode (= a named place) or with geographic coordinates. For mobility data portals, usage of geocodes is preferred. As geocodes, IRIs from predefined controlled vocabularies should be used, such as the EU Authority Table "Continent", the EU Authority Table "Countries and territories", the EU Authority Table "Places", the GeoNames geographical database, the EU Taxonomy "Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics" (NUTS).
spatial_coverage.title: Area covered

distributions.title: Distributions
distributions.description: A distribution describes the data formats and communication methods for a dataset. There may be one or multiple distributions for one dataset. For example, the same dataset (e.g. static parking information for truck drivers) can be provided in different ways e.g. as downloadable zip file or as XML using a REST web service. These are two distributions based on one dataset.

data_schema.title: Data schema/model
data_schema.description: The mobility data standard, as applied for the delivered content within the distribution. A mobility data standard, e.g., DATEX II, combines syntax and semantic definitions of entities in a certain domain (e.g., for DATEX II: road traffic information), and optionally adds technical rules for data exchange. Select from the mobilitydcatap:mobilityDataStandard vocabulary. If no suitable standard is found in this vocabulary, the "other" entry should be used.

format.title: Resource format
format.description: The technical syntax of the delivered content within the distribution. It describes the base standard that specifies syntactically correct documents. On this level, base elements are properly specified on how to build a document. The resulting document can then be validated by syntax checks. Select from the EU Publications Office file-type authority vocabulary.

rights.title: Rights
rights.description: The rights associated with the distribution. In particular, a statement about the intellectual property rights (IPR). As a minimum, it should include an information on the type of conditions for access and usage. Select from the mobilitydcatap:conditions-for-access-and-usage vocabulary.

access_url.title: Access URL
access_url.description: A URL that gives access to a distribution of the dataset. Depending on the type of data provision, there are different options for describing the URL. For data services, e.g., API, broker services, data feeds, etc., the URL may be the end point of such service. If some agreements between the data provider and the data user need to be established first, the access URL may link to web page, where the access is further arranged, e.g., initiating a subscription process. For data which can be downloaded directly, the URL should be a direct link to a downloadable file in a given format. For other cases, where data cannot be directly accessed or downloaded via the platform, the access URL may be a link to an external service or a website which enables access to the data.
